newsitem.title: GERMANY: Audi says creates about 1,000 new jobs in Germany.
newsitem.headline: Audi says creates about 1,000 new jobs in Germany.

text.p: German carmaker Audi AG, bucking the industry trend to cut domestic jobs, said on Tuesday it added some 1,000 new full-time workers in Germany last year to match increased demand for its luxury vehicles.

Audi, a unit of Volkswagen AG , said its workforce in Germany rose 4.6 percent to 34,204 workers as car production rose about 10 percent to 491,500 vehicles. In addition to the full-time jobs, Audi said it added 500 more part-time workers.

The move by Audi, which reported record sales of 18.8 billion marks last year, to create jobs in Germany stands in contrast to other carmakers who have kept payrolls steady or shed German jobs in favour of lower-cost countries.

Audi plans to build a factory in Brazil with Volkswagen to begin producing in 1998 its A3 subcompact vehicle, marking the carmaker's first full step into production outside of Germany. But the carmaker has vowed to maintain its German workforce.
Audi also added jobs in foreign countries, particularly at its engine production plant in Gyoer, Hungary, with the carmaker's global workforce rising 6.7 percent to 35,215.
Some of the new jobs were needed to meet increasing demand for the A3, which has caught on well in the marketplace in addition to Audi's popular A4 saloon.
The carmaker said more than 52,000 of the A3 three-door vehicles have been built since September.
"We have naturally more production with the A3 and needed more workers," an Audi spokesman said. "Other models are also selling very well and the orders must be met."
In addition, Audi said engine production in Germany and Hungary rose 2.2 percent to 620,603 units last year, prompting the need for about 700 additional jobs.

Audi did not provide profit figures in a statement issued on Tuesday but has previously said it expected pre-tax profit to be up a minimum 25 percent. Audi in 1995 reported a profit from ordinary activities of 589 million marks.
